facts.fact: The African Union Infrastructure and Energy Department says Equatorial Guinea's foreign minister signed the Malabo Convention (AU Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection) on 28 July 2026 in Addis Ababa, calling it a step towards ratification and implementation.
Revista Real Equatorial Guinea reports that on 25 March 2026 the Chamber of Deputies unanimously approved ratification of the Malabo Convention; it says nothing of an instrument being deposited.

The government press office reports that on 25 March 2026 the plenary of the Chamber of Deputies approved by unanimity the proposal to ratify the African Union Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection, on the report of the parliamentary foreign policy and treaties committee; it says nothing of deposit.

The African Union Commission's status list dated 2 February 2026 shows no date of signature, ratification or deposit against Equatorial Guinea for the Malabo Convention (21 signatures and 20 ratifications among 55 states).

note: Only a 19 Nov 2025 interministerial council proposal to authorise the Malabo Convention, a proposal not a signature, ratification or statement of absence.

facts.fact: The Data Protection Africa fact sheet by ALT Advisory lists the Malabo Convention as 'No' under Equatorial Guinea's international commitments; the page was last updated 24 June 2022 and the date is taken from that.

note: The passages file holds no paragraph naming Equatorial Guinea; the ingest note's ratification date comes from elsewhere and is not taken.
The framework is a validated regional document, not a signed or ratified legal text.

facts.fact: ACTPOL, citing the African Union status list of 2 February 2026, says Equatorial Guinea has taken no action on the Malabo Convention.
